pool.text: The Grand National Assembly of Turkey was established in Ankara on April 23.
Ankara became the new Turkish capital upon the establishment of the Republic.
Ankara had about 35,000 residents in the year after the government moved.
The population of Ankara reached 44,553 residents according to records.
The Security Monument was erected in Güvenpark near Kızılay Square bearing advice.
The population of Ankara had grown to 286,781 residents in the city.
The Monument to Turkish Soldiers Fighting in Korea opened to commemorate veterans.
The Hatti Monument was erected at Sıhhiye Square to symbolize the Hatti Sun Disc.
The State Art and Sculpture Museum opened to the public near the Ethnography Museum.
Galeri Siyah Beyaz was founded as a well-known art gallery in Ankara.
Çankaya Çağdaş Sanatlar Merkezi Concert Hall was founded as a performing arts center.
The Roman Road of Ankara or Cardo Maximus was found by Cevdet Bayburtluoğlu.
The Colored Angora Goat Breeders Association was set up to promote colored Angoras.
Hacettepe Symphony Orchestra was founded and directed by Erol Erdinç.
Cermodern was inaugurated as the modern-arts museum of Ankara on April 1.
The Mehmet Akif Literature Museum Library opened as an important literary archive.
The THF Sport Hall was built to host Handball Super League matches.
A large new mosque in the Turkish neoclassical style was completed and opened.
A few more shopping malls were open in Ankara during this year.
The city was one of the sites of the coup attempt on July 15.
